article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 70% Indica / 30% Sativa
Genetics: OG Kush
Breeder: DNA Genetics
THC Content: 20–25%
CBD Content: Generally below 1%
Terpene Profile: myrcene , limonene , beta-caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Lemon, citrus peel, pine, diesel, earth
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: October
Indoor Yield: 400–500 grams per square meter
Outdoor Yield: Moderate
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Florida OG belongs to the period of cannabis history when a single exceptional clone could carry more prestige than an elaborate pedigree. Long before every dispensary menu contained dozens of OG descendants, Florida growers were circulating powerful, sharp-smelling marijuana that became associated with names such as Crippy and, later, OG Kush.

DNA Genetics eventually preserved and released a coveted Florida cutting through its Grow Your Own collection, describing it as the classic OG from which an enormous family of later crosses emerged. The flower captures nearly every quality people associate with traditional OG weed: penetrating lemon, damp earth, pine resin, fuel, dense trichome coverage, moderate yields, and an effect that combines an immediate mental lift with substantial physical relaxation.
Genetics and Lineage

Florida OG has one of those cannabis pedigrees where restraint is more accurate than a perfectly drawn family tree. DNA Genetics did not identify its seed release as Chemdawg × Lemon Thai × Hindu Kush or any other precise cross. Its own catalog simply calls the genetic source a “Coveted Cutting” and classifies the cultivar as 70% indica and 30% sativa. DNA also associated the cut with the names Florida OG, Crippy, and Ocean Grown and promoted it as an original expression of classic OG cannabis. The breeder’s catalog gives nine weeks of flowering and 400–500 grams per square meter as its core cultivation specifications.

A widely repeated theory places OG Kush ancestry somewhere around Chemdawg, Lemon Thai, and Pakistani or Hindu Kush genetics. That reconstruction may describe the broader OG family, but it should not be presented as documented parentage for DNA’s Florida cutting. The original underground movement of these clones occurred before widespread genetic testing or formal pedigree records, and competing stories remain part of OG Kush history. In a reference guide, the most defensible lineage is therefore the one the breeder actually supplied: an elite Florida OG clone from the foundational OG Kush gene pool.

Its influence can be traced more confidently through descendants than through ancestors. DNA Genetics subsequently used Florida OG in projects such as Florida Gold and Florida Lemons, demonstrating that the cut was valued as breeding material rather than simply released as another commercial strain. The reason is easy to understand: the plant carries a recognizable combination of vigor, resin, potency, citrus-fuel aroma, and classic OG flower structure even though yield is not its strongest attribute.
Effects and Experience

The first few minutes often feel more animated than the indica-heavy classification suggests. Mental pressure builds quickly behind the eyes, mood rises, and attention can become unusually absorbed in conversation, music, games, or creative work. Instead of producing immediate lethargy, the early phase has enough brightness to feel functional in moderate amounts. That cerebral movement is one of the qualities that separates classic OG marijuana from simpler heavy-bodied Kush varieties.

Relaxation begins to take over as the high develops. Muscles loosen, physical tension becomes less noticeable, and the initially active headspace settles into a calmer rhythm. A strong dose can produce considerable body weight without necessarily erasing the euphoric mental component. For experienced consumers, this combination can make the cultivar suitable for the transition between an active day and a quieter evening.

Potency should not be underestimated. Modern Florida OG flower commonly appears around the low-to-mid 20% THC range, though there is no universal breeder-certified percentage. Large doses may lead to dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, short-term memory disruption, anxiety, or eventual sleepiness. The strain’s reputation was built on strength long before THC numbers became a central marketing tool.
Medical Benefits

Medical marijuana consumers sometimes choose OG-family cannabis for the combination of mood elevation and substantial physical relaxation. With Florida OG, the early cerebral component may temporarily make everyday stress feel less intrusive, while the heavier stage can appeal to people dealing with bodily tension or discomfort. Appetite can also increase as the experience progresses, especially at stronger doses.

Evening consumers may find the later relaxation useful when discomfort or mental tension makes it difficult to settle down. At the same time, its relatively lively onset means it does not always behave like a straightforward sleep strain. Some individuals remain mentally engaged for a considerable period before sedation appears, while others find a larger dose strongly calming.

These uses remain experiential rather than strain-specific medical proof. Controlled trials have not demonstrated that Florida OG treats insomnia, anxiety, PTSD, chronic pain, depression, or another particular condition. Anyone using high-THC weed medicinally should consider the laboratory analysis of the actual batch and discuss cannabis with a qualified healthcare professional when prescription medication or significant medical conditions are involved.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Classic OG character defines the nose. A properly cured bud often opens with sharp lemon peel and pine before a deeper layer of fuel, damp soil, herbs, and pepper moves forward. Grinding the flower dramatically increases the pungency, creating the unmistakable mixture of citrus cleaner, evergreen resin, and gasoline that helped make OG-derived cannabis famous. There may be subtle sweetness, but this is not a dessert strain .

On the palate, lemon and pine tend to arrive before earth and diesel. The exhale can become considerably heavier, leaving behind a spicy, resinous Kush flavor with a lingering fuel edge. Certain batches show more citrus; others lean toward musk, pine, or pepper. That variation is expected from an old clone circulated through different cultivation environments.

Modern laboratory examples support a terpene spectrum that can include myrcene, limonene, beta-caryophyllene, and additional secondary compounds. One tested Florida OG batch analyzed by Kaycha Labs contained myrcene, limonene, and beta-caryophyllene among its leading terpenes, reinforcing the earthy, citrus, and spicy profile commonly associated with the cultivar. Terpene percentages should still be considered batch-specific rather than universal.
Growing Information

Florida OG has excellent breeding qualities but is not famous for effortless commercial production. DNA Genetics specifically praised its growth, vigor, structure, aroma, appearance, and strength while acknowledging that very large yields can be difficult to achieve. The official catalog lists approximately 400–500 grams per square meter and nine weeks of flowering, placing the plant in the moderate-yield category rather than among modern production-focused hybrids.

Vegetative growth can be vigorous, and plants may stretch noticeably after the flowering cycle begins. Branches benefit from support as dense, resinous flowers gain weight. Rather than producing enormous uniform colas with little effort, OG-type plants often reward careful canopy management and consistent environmental control. Mature buds become hard and trichome-rich, with a strong aroma appearing well before harvest.

Outdoor maturity generally arrives during October in climates where autumn remains reasonably warm and dry. Dense marijuana flowers become more vulnerable when prolonged humidity or rainfall coincides with the final weeks of bloom, making airflow and weather conditions important considerations. Outdoor production can be respectable, but DNA Genetics never promoted the cut as a mass-yield variety; flower quality and breeding value were always the stronger attractions.
FAQ
Is Florida OG indica or sativa?

Florida OG is an indica-dominant hybrid. DNA Genetics lists the cultivar as approximately 70% indica and 30% sativa. Despite that classification, the high can begin with a surprisingly energetic and cerebral quality before deeper physical relaxation develops.
What are the real genetics of Florida OG?

DNA Genetics officially describes Florida OG only as a “Coveted Cutting.” The breeder did not publish a conventional two-parent pedigree. Although Chemdawg, Lemon Thai, and Hindu Kush are frequently mentioned in discussions of OG Kush ancestry, that combination should not be treated as confirmed parentage for the Florida OG release.
Is Florida OG the same as Crippy?

DNA Genetics used Florida OG, Crippy, and Ocean Grown when describing its cultivar. Historically, however, “crippy” was also used more broadly in Florida for high-quality marijuana, so not every cannabis product called Crippy necessarily represents the same clone.
How strong is Florida OG weed?

Modern batches commonly fall somewhere around 20–25% THC, with roughly 22% frequently reported. Actual potency depends on cultivation, phenotype, harvest maturity, and testing methodology. Consumers should rely on the laboratory result for their specific flower rather than assuming every sample has identical THC content.
How long does Florida OG take to flower?

DNA Genetics gives the strain an indoor flowering period of approximately nine weeks, or about 63 days. Outdoor plants generally mature during October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates. Indoor yields are officially listed around 400–500 grams per square meter under favorable conditions.
Final Thoughts on Florida OG

Florida OG is important less because of a tidy pedigree than because of what the clone represents. DNA Genetics preserved it as a coveted Florida cutting associated with the earliest OG Kush tradition, and its traits read like a blueprint for the family that followed: lemon and pine over fuel and earth, dense resinous flowers, substantial potency, moderate production, and an effect that combines cerebral elevation with physical calm.

For cannabis enthusiasts interested in the history behind modern OG weed, that authenticity gives this marijuana strain unusual relevance. It does not need candy flavors, enormous harvests, or a complicated genetic name to stand apart. Florida OG built its reputation on aroma, resin, strength, and the unmistakable structure of classic Kush cannabis. Even with uncertainty surrounding its deeper ancestry, the cultivar remains an important reference point for understanding how Florida’s underground marijuana genetics helped shape the broader OG family.
